_comment: Operator questionnaire for packer/pack_bundle.py -- the same information the TopSpin dialogs collect, as one JSON file. Copy to answers.json, edit, then run: python3 packer/pack_bundle.py <data_dir> --answers answers.json. Keys starting with _ are ignored.
_run_mode_choices: external-acquisition (real data acquired with the vendor's own software) | archival-repackage (historical data) | desktest / simulate (plumbing tests, never science data)

environment._field_sweep_note: Bruker: did you verify on the BSMS display that the FIELD SWEEP was OFF during the noise block? A running sweep smears the noise feature by kHz and ruins the record.

spectrometer._temperature_note: PHYSICAL temperatures in kelvin, null if unknown. Room-temperature probe: the coil sits at the probe-body temperature, i.e. the lab ambient, and the preamp at its own physical ambient -- a measured lab temperature (e.g. 296.5) beats an assumed 298. Corrections learned later go to the maintainer as numbers, not as a re-upload.
spectrometer._h1_freq_mhz: usually read from the vendor files (Bruker acqus BF1); uncomment to override

instrument._note: vendor-specific answers; for vendor=jeol supply delta_version, for vendor=magritek supply spinsolve_software_version (those readers are drafts pending partner/bench validation); for vendor=agilent supply vnmrj_version or copy /vnmr/vnmrrev into the session directory

calibration._rg_ladder_note: one entry per rung IN ACQUISITION ORDER; the same rg may appear more than once (the randomized repeated ladder: each level visited three times in random order) and nothing sorts or dedups the list. Omit rg_ladder entirely to have the packer build it from the rg_ladder experiments' stored gains (tip_deg from reference_tip_deg, default 1.0); with no ladder experiments either, a single-entry ladder is taken from a reference experiment and the limitation flagged.

_experiments_note: one entry per expno: 'role' is one of setup | rg_ladder | reference_open | noise | reference_close | noise_tune | sweep_signcal. For vendor=agilent the Tier-1 save-name suffix implies the role (NN_sn_ladder, _sn_ref_open, _sn_noise, _sn_ref_close, _sn_tune_k, _sn_signcal; the role word may be followed by anything but a letter, so 17_sn_noise2 reads as noise and 17_sn_noisetest reads as nothing), so only entries that add information need listing; an entry's role overrides the name. Acquisition parameters (td, td1_rows, sw_hz, o1_hz, rg, ns, started_local, finished_local) are read from the vendor files where possible; anything the files lack must be added here.
_experiments_agilent_example_note: what the tuning-ladder and axis-sign entries of an Agilent session look like (quickstart 2.6-2.7); move them into 'experiments' for such a session. They sit under an ignored _ key here so that this Bruker-flavoured template packs a Bruker session without 'describes expno N but the data directory has no such experiment' WARNs.
_tuning_note: OPTIONAL per-experiment 'tuning' object (spin-noise tuning ladder, v0.7.1), passed through verbatim: setting_index (integer >= 0, REQUIRED; 0 = the operator's normal tuning), label (text), tune_reading and match_reading (whatever numbers the console shows, or null), units (names them), note. No other keys. noise_tune blocks are grouped by setting_index and never co-added with the headline noise block; an Agilent save named NN_sn_tune_k supplies setting_index k when this object is absent.
_sweep_signcal_note: sweep_signcal: one extra small-flip 1D with the transmitter carrier displaced by a known amount (Agilent: tof + 200 Hz), same pulse/gain/record length as the references. The packer records o1_hz from the vendor files; the report takes o1_hz(signcal) - o1_hz(reference) as the displacement and resolves the frequency-axis sign from where the line moved (physical convention: its apparent in-window offset DROPS by the displacement).
